passages.text: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, like some people, letters of recommendation to you or from you?
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul speaks to the believers in Corinth.
Paul asks a question.
Paul says, "Are we starting to praise ourselves again?"
Paul asks another question.
Paul says, "Do we need letters of recommendation to you?"
Paul says, "Do we need letters of recommendation from you?"
Some people use letters of recommendation.
Paul and his companions do not need such letters.
passages.original: Ἀρχόμεθα πάλιν ἑαυτοὺς συνιστάνειν ἢ μὴ χρῄζομεν ὥς τινες συστατικῶν ἐπιστολῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἢ ἐξ ὑμῶν

passages.text: You yourselves are our letter, inscribed on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul writes to the believers in Corinth.
You are the people Paul addresses.
You are like a letter from Paul and his companions.
Paul and his companions carry you in their hearts.
Everyone can see your faith.
Everyone can understand your lives.
People know and read your example.
passages.original: ἡ ἐπιστολὴ ἡμῶν ὑμεῖς ἐστε ἐνγεγραμμένη ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν γινωσκομένη καὶ ἀναγινωσκομένη ὑπὸ πάντων ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: It is clear that you are a letter from Christ, the result of our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.
passages.sermon:
You are a letter from Christ.
Christ sent you as His message.
We served as ministers for Christ.
God wrote this letter through us.
God did not use ink to write this letter.
God used the Spirit of the living God to write it.
God did not write this letter on tablets of stone.
God wrote this letter on tablets of human hearts.
passages.original: φανερούμενοι ὅτι ἐστὲ ἐπιστολὴ Χριστοῦ διακονηθεῖσα ὑφ’ ἡμῶν ἐνγεγραμμένη οὐ μέλανι ἀλλὰ Πνεύματι Θεοῦ ζῶντος οὐκ ἐν πλαξὶν λιθίναις ἀλλ’ ἐν πλαξὶν καρδίαις σαρκίναις

passages.text: Such confidence before God is ours through Christ.
passages.sermon: We have confidence before God.\r\nChrist gives us this confidence.
passages.original: Πεποίθησιν δὲ τοιαύτην ἔχομεν διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim that anything comes from us, but our competence comes from God.
passages.sermon: We are not competent by ourselves.\r\nWe cannot claim that anything comes from us.\r\nGod gives us our competence.
passages.original: οὐχ ὅτι ἀφ’ ἑαυτῶν ἱκανοί ἐσμεν λογίσασθαί τι ὡς ἐξ ἑαυτῶν ἀλλ’ ἡ ἱκανότης ἡμῶν ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: And He has qualified us as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
passages.sermon:
God has made us able to serve.
We serve as ministers of a new covenant.
This new covenant does not come from the letter.
This new covenant comes from the Spirit.
The letter brings death.
The Spirit gives life.
passages.original: ὃς καὶ ἱκάνωσεν ἡμᾶς διακόνους καινῆς διαθήκης οὐ γράμματος ἀλλὰ πνεύματος τὸ γὰρ γράμμα ἀποκτέννει τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζωοποιεῖ

passages.text: Now if the ministry of death, which was engraved in letters on stone, came with such glory that the Israelites could not gaze at the face of Moses because of its fleeting glory, will not the ministry of the Spirit be even more glorious?
passages.sermon:
The ministry of death was written in letters on stone.
God gave this ministry to Israel.
This ministry came with great glory.
The Israelites saw the glory on Moses’ face.
The Israelites could not look at Moses’ face.
The glory on Moses’ face was fading away.
The ministry of the Spirit comes from God.
The ministry of the Spirit is even more glorious.
passages.original: Εἰ δὲ ἡ διακονία τοῦ θανάτου ἐν γράμμασιν ἐντετυπωμένη λίθοις ἐγενήθη ἐν δόξῃ ὥστε μὴ δύνασθαι ἀτενίσαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον Μωϋσέως διὰ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ τὴν καταργουμένην πῶς οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἡ διακονία τοῦ πνεύματος ἔσται ἐν δόξῃ

passages.text: For if the ministry of condemnation was glorious, how much more glorious is the ministry of righteousness!
passages.sermon:
The ministry of condemnation had glory.
The ministry of condemnation brought judgment.
The ministry of righteousness brings something greater.
The ministry of righteousness is much more glorious.
The ministry of righteousness surpasses the ministry of condemnation in glory.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ τῇ διακονία τῆς κατακρίσεως δόξα πολλῷ μᾶλλον περισσεύει ἡ διακονία τῆς δικαιοσύνης δόξῃ

passages.text: Indeed, what was once glorious has no glory now in comparison to the glory that surpasses it.
passages.sermon:
Something was once glorious.
Now, it does not have glory.
A greater glory has come.
The new glory is much greater than the old glory.
The old glory cannot compare to the new, surpassing glory.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ οὐ δεδόξασται τὸ δεδοξασμένον ἐν τούτῳ τῷ μέρει εἵνεκεν τῆς ὑπερβαλλούσης δόξης

passages.text: For if what was fading away came with glory, how much greater is the glory of that which endures!
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking about two ministries.
\r\nThe first ministry was temporary.
\r\nThis ministry was fading away.
\r\nGod gave this ministry with glory.
\r\nThe second ministry remains forever.
\r\nThis ministry endures.
\r\nGod gives this ministry with much greater glory.
\r\nThe glory of the enduring ministry is far greater than the glory of the fading ministry.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ τὸ καταργούμενον διὰ δόξης πολλῷ μᾶλλον τὸ μένον ἐν δόξῃ

passages.text: Therefore, since we have such a hope, we are very bold.
passages.sermon:
We have this hope.
This hope is great.
Because of this hope, we speak with boldness.
We act with confidence.
We do not hide our message.
passages.original: Ἔχοντες οὖν τοιαύτην ἐλπίδα πολλῇ παρρησίᾳ χρώμεθα

passages.text: We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away.
passages.sermon:
We are not like Moses.
Moses put a veil over his face.
He did this to keep the Israelites from looking at his face.
He wanted to stop them from seeing the end of what was fading away.
passages.original: καὶ οὐ καθάπερ Μωϋσῆς ἐτίθει κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἀτενίσαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ εἰς τὸ τέλος τοῦ καταργουμένου

passages.text: But their minds were closed. For to this day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant. It has not been lifted, because only in Christ can it be removed.
passages.sermon:
Their minds were closed.
This happened to the people of Israel.
To this day, the same veil remains when people read the old covenant.
The veil has not been lifted.
Only Christ can remove the veil.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ ἐπωρώθη τὰ νοήματα αὐτῶν ἄχρι γὰρ τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας τὸ αὐτὸ κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τῇ ἀναγνώσει τῆς παλαιᾶς διαθήκης μένει μὴ ἀνακαλυπτόμενον ὅτι ἐν Χριστῷ καταργεῖται

passages.text: And even to this day when Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes about the people of Israel.
Their hearts remain covered by a veil.
This happens even today.
Whenever someone reads the writings of Moses, the veil stays over their hearts.
The veil prevents them from understanding.
This continues until now.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ ἕως σήμερον ἡνίκα ἂν ἀναγινώσκηται Μωϋσῆς κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτῶν κεῖται

passages.text: But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
passages.sermon:
Anyone can turn to the Lord.
When a person turns to the Lord, God removes the veil.
The veil no longer covers that person.
God takes away what blocked understanding.
passages.original: ἡνίκα δὲ ἐὰν ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς Κύριον περιαιρεῖται τὸ κάλυμμα

passages.text: Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
passages.sermon: The Lord is the Spirit.\r\nThe Spirit belongs to the Lord.\r\nWhere the Spirit of the Lord is present, there is freedom.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Κύριος τὸ Πνεῦμά ἐστιν οὗ δὲ τὸ Πνεῦμα Κυρίου ἐλευθερία

passages.text: And we, who with unveiled faces all reflect the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
passages.sermon:
We are followers of Jesus Christ.
We have turned to the Lord.
God has removed the veil from our faces.
We see the glory of the Lord clearly.
We reflect the Lord’s glory.
The Lord is the Spirit.
The Spirit of the Lord works in us.
The Spirit transforms us.
We are changed into the image of the Lord.
We become more and more like Him.
Our transformation grows from one degree of glory to another.
This change comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
passages.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ πάντες ἀνακεκαλυμμένῳ προσώπῳ τὴν δόξαν Κυρίου κατοπτριζόμενοι τὴν αὐτὴν εἰκόνα μεταμορφούμεθα ἀπὸ δόξης εἰς δόξαν καθάπερ ἀπὸ Κυρίου Πνεύματος
